summary: Sauk R.S. (the Lookout Tree), Snohomish County: a 1918 crow's nest in a cedar, abandoned in the 1930s; sources say the tree is still there.

facts.design: crow's nest in a cedar tree, with spikes driven into the trunk as steps
facts.status_note: Abandoned as a fire lookout; firelookout.com says it is 'Still there' and the Firelookout.org index lists it as Abandoned, not gone.

access.note: WTA describes the Lookout Tree trail (#783.1) as a short, no longer maintained section of trail; WTA advises hikers to use caution.

visit.trail_note: WTA describes the trail as a short, no longer maintained section. Willhite gives the trailhead as 11.3 miles south of Darrington on the Mountain Loop Highway.

events.note: Crow's nest built atop a cedar; spikes driven into the trunk for climbing.
Sauk River Timber Company put a train through; supplies began arriving by train instead of pack train.

evidence.supports: Crow's nest in an 11-foot DBH cedar, built 1918; abandoned 1930s; still there
evidence.quote: 1918: crow's nest in 11' DBH cedar. Abandoned 1930s. Still there.

evidence.supports: Index lists Sauk R.S. as Abandoned
Lookout built 1918 from a huge cedar
evidence.quote: Built in 1918, a huge cedar tree was made into a fire lookout.

evidence.supports: Beside the Sauk River, near the Sauk Guard Station
evidence.quote: located along the river bottom near the Sauk Guard Station

evidence.supports: Crow's nest on top; spikes as steps
evidence.quote: A crows nest was constructed on the top
During fire season this tree was climbed daily to look for signs of fire.
The only way to get supplies into the area was by pack train.
When Sauk River Timber Company put the train through in 1926, supplies arrived by train.

evidence.supports: Abandoned as a fire lookout in the 1930s
evidence.quote: In the 1930s the Lookout Tree was abandoned as a fire lookout.

drive 11.3 miles from the Darrington south on the Mountain Loop Highway

evidence.quote: a short, no longer maintained section of trail
Hikers who want to visit should use caution.

evidence.supports: Tree described as 75 feet in diameter
Sauk Guard Station tree; cedar; crow's nest; pegs for a ladder
evidence.quote: Established atop a cedar tree. Pegs were driven into the tree trunk for a ladder and a crows nest built at the top.

corrections.why: Firelookout.com says the tree is 'Still there' and the Firelookout.org index lists the site as Abandoned; neither calls it gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com calls it Sauk R.S.; Washington Lookouts calls it Sauk Guard Station (tree); Willhite calls it the Lookout Tree near the Sauk Guard Station. Dates and materials agree (1918, cedar, crow's nest, abandoned in the 1930s), so the story treats them as one site. No source says so directly.
Firelookout.com gives 11 ft DBH, Willhite gives 15 ft, and WTA gives 75 ft. The story reports all three and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Identity is inferred: Firelookout.com's Sauk R.S. (1918 cedar crow's nest, abandoned 1930s) matches Willhite's and Washington Lookouts' Sauk Guard Station / Lookout Tree, but no source equates them. Brief status 'gone' is not supported; Firelookout.com says 'Still there' (undated) and the index says Abandoned. Width conflict: 11 ft DBH vs 15 ft vs WTA's 75 ft (likely an error, not resolved). Trail length conflict unrecorded: Willhite says 1/2 mile, WTA says 0.6 miles roundtrip. Abandonment has no single year, so no abandoned event. Six page reads used; two WebSearch calls used. The Sauk Ranger Station (WTA search snippet, built 1916) was not read and is not used.
